definition: An FTR option is a variant of the FTR contract where one party pays an up-front premium to avoid ever having to pay congestion charges, rather than taking on a two-way obligation.
core_idea: Buying an FTR option functions like buying insurance against higher prices caused by congestion — the buyer's downside is capped at the premium paid, unlike a standard obligation-style FTR where either side can end up paying.
key_points: Structured as an option rather than an obligation: buyer pays a premium up front.
Protects the buyer only from paying on congestion charges (asymmetric protection vs. the two-way obligation FTR).
relationships: Derived from / structured as a variant of the base FTR obligation contract.
trading_implications: Preferred over a standard FTR obligation when a party wants defined, capped downside (premium only) rather than open-ended two-way congestion payment risk.
